Q57402.label: Daniel Ortega
Q57402.summary: José Daniel Ortega Saavedra is a Nicaraguan politician, revolutionary, and former guerrilla fighter who, under various titles, has been the leader of Nicaragua since 2007 and previously from 1979 to 1990.

Q706106.label: Pierre Frieden
Q706106.img: Jean-Pierre Beckius, Portrait du professeur Frieden (1933).jpg
Q706106.summary: Pierre Frieden was a Luxembourgish politician and writer. He was prime minister of Luxembourg, serving for eleven months, from 29 March 1958 until his death, on 23 February 1959. He also served as Interior Minister from 1951.

Q2189370.label: 1936 French legislative election
Q2189370.summary: Legislative elections were held in France on 26 April and 3 May 1936, the last elections before World War II. The number of candidates set a record, with 4,807 running for election to the Chamber of Deputies. In the Seine Department alone, there were 1,402 candidates. The legislative election was the last before women were granted the right to vote in April 1944.

Q2679354.label: 1991 Soviet Union referendum
Q2679354.desc: referendum regarding the dissolution of the Soviet Union
Q2679354.summary: A referendum on the future of the Soviet Union was held on 17 March 1991 across the Soviet Union. It was the only national referendum in the history of the Soviet Union, although it was boycotted by authorities in six of the fifteen Soviet republics.

Q1626682.label: 1958 Finnish parliamentary election
Q1626682.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Finland on 6 and 7 July 1958. The Finnish People's Democratic League, which was dominated by the Communist Party of Finland, emerged as the largest party, but was unable to form a government.

Q83002.label: First Battle of al-Faw
Q83002.summary: The First Battle of al-Faw was a battle of the Iran–Iraq War, fought on the al-Faw peninsula between 10 February and 10 March 1986. The Iranian operation is considered to be one of Iran's greatest achievements in the Iran–Iraq War.

Q83514.label: Alpine Convention
Q83514.desc: international treaty for the sustainable development of the Alps
Q83514.summary: The Alpine Convention (AC), formally the Convention on the Protection of the Alps, is an international treaty on the comprehensive protection and sustainable development of the Alps. The Convention is a pioneer of its kind as the first international treaty covering a whole mountain range that crosses several national borders.

Q50842170.label: Carcassonne and Trèbes attack
Q50842170.summary: On 23 March 2018, an Islamic terrorist carried out three attacks in the town of Carcassonne and the nearby village of Trèbes in the Aude department in southwestern France, killing four people and injuring fifteen.

Q853562.label: libertarian conservatism
Q853562.summary: Libertarian conservatism, also referred to as conservative libertarianism and, more rarely, conservatarianism, is a libertarian political and social philosophy that combines conservatism and libertarianism, representing the libertarian wing of conservatism and vice versa.

Q2165306.label: People's Alliance
Q2165306.summary: The People's Alliance was an electoral alliance in Iceland from 1956 to 1968 and a socialist political party from 1968 to 1998.
